references.text: Confirmation of Ruth's identity and return from Moab as the basis for her integration into Bethlehem.
Ruth's identity as a Moabite widow is theologically transformed from social status to a means of salvation for the family inheritance.
The contrast between Naomi's urging to return (1:15) and Ruth's actual return (1:22) highlights Ruth's loyalty.
Temporal and theological connection between the arrival at the start of harvest and Ruth's immediate action to receive God's provision.
Development of the relationship from Ruth's arrival as a daughter-in-law to Naomi's active protection of her in the fields during harvest.
Narrative circle: The departure from Moab (1:6) and the arrival in Bethlehem (1:22) mark the beginning and end of God's guidance of Naomi.
Ruth's identity as a foreigner from Moab (1:22) is theologically elevated to become a means of salvation for the family inheritance (4:10).
The contrast between Naomi's urging to leave (1:8) and Ruth's actual choice to go with her (1:22) shows Ruth's unwavering loyalty.
From Ruth's arrival as a widow (1:22) to the birth of the heir (4:13), which fulfills God's promise to raise up the name of the dead.
